title: Trend definition and categories
claim: Uptrend: series of higher highs and higher lows; Downtrend: series of lower highs and lower lows; Sideways: price oscillates without clear direction
support: Pring defines and illustrates all three trend types
validation: Verify against historical OHLC data

title: Trend reversal identification
claim: Trend reversal occurs when series of higher highs/lows breaks; must maintain investment posture until weight of evidence indicates reversal
support: Core TA principle stated in introduction and Chapter 1
mechanism: Price breaks pattern; new pattern establishes
validation: Count bars until next higher/lower high/low confirmed

title: Dow Theory: three trends
claim: Dow Theory identifies Primary trend (1-5 years), Intermediate trend (6 weeks-1 year), Secondary trend (under 6 weeks)
support: Pring explains multi-timeframe trend hierarchy
mechanism: Markets move in multiple concurrent timeframes
validation: Identify trends at multiple timeframes on same chart

title: Support and resistance zones
claim: Support: price level where demand stops declines; Resistance: level where supply stops advances; levels identified from swing lows and highs
support: Pring defines and illustrates support/resistance with historical examples
validation: Identify prior swing points and measure reversal frequency at levels

title: Trendline as dynamic support/resistance
claim: Trendline connects swing lows in uptrend and highs in downtrend; acts as dynamic support/resistance; break signals potential reversal
support: Pring explains trendline construction and interpretation
validation: Backtest: count reversals at trendline break vs baseline

title: Volume confirms price trend
claim: Rising volume during uptrend confirms strength; declining volume during uptrend suggests weakening; volume reversal at trend break is bullish
support: Pring explains volume-price relationship
validation: Compute volume SMA and compare to price changes

title: Head and shoulders pattern
claim: Head and shoulders (HS): left shoulder, head higher, right shoulder symmetric to left; neckline break confirms reversal; target = HS height
support: Pring illustrates HS pattern formation and price target calculation
mechanism: Distribution at resistance; break of neckline triggers selling
validation: Identify HS patterns and measure win rate and payoff ratio

title: Double and triple tops/bottoms
claim: Double top: two peaks at similar level; reversal on break below support between peaks; Double bottom: two troughs; reversal on break above
support: Pring explains double/triple formations
validation: Backtest double-top short entry + risk/reward

title: Moving average: trend filter and signal
claim: MA(n) smooths price; MA crossover signals trend change; price above MA = uptrend, below = downtrend; common periods: 10, 50, 200
support: Pring explains MA construction, interpretation, and typical periods
validation: Compare MA(10/50/200) to price action; measure lag on reversals

title: MA lag at reversals
claim: MAs lag during sharp reversals; golden cross/death cross can occur after significant price move already underway; late to reversals
support: Pring acknowledges MA lag in fast-moving markets
mechanism: MA averages historical prices; ignores recent momentum
validation: Measure entry delay (bars) between price reversal and MA crossover

title: Bollinger Bands: volatility and overbought/oversold
claim: Bands = SMA +/- 2*StDev; price at upper band = overbought (mean reversion likely); lower band = oversold; band width reflects volatility
support: Pring explains BB construction and interpretation
validation: Backtest: sell when price > upper band; buy when < lower band

title: Momentum oscillators: RSI basics
claim: RSI = 100 - 100/(1+RS); RS = avg gain/avg loss over n periods; RSI > 70 = overbought, < 30 = oversold; n typically 14
support: Pring explains RSI formula and interpretation
validation: Backtest RSI > 70 short, RSI < 30 long signals

title: RSI whipsaws in strong trends
claim: RSI can remain overbought in strong uptrend or oversold in downtrend for extended periods; does not guarantee reversal
support: Pring cautions against relying solely on RSI extremes
mechanism: Strong momentum can override oscillator signals
validation: Measure false reversal rate when RSI in extreme zone but price continues trend

title: MACD: trend plus momentum
claim: MACD = EMA(12) - EMA(26); Signal = EMA(9) of MACD; Histogram = MACD - Signal; crossover signals trend change
support: Pring explains MACD construction
mechanism: Exponential MA convergence/divergence captures trend momentum
validation: Test MACD crossover signals vs price crossover

title: Stochastic: momentum within bounds
claim: Stochastic = 100*(close-low14)/(high14-low14); %K smoothed by SMA; %K > 80 = overbought, < 20 = oversold; good for range-bound markets
support: Pring explains Stochastic formula and application
validation: Backtest Stochastic crossover signals; measure win rate in trending vs choppy markets

title: Candlestick patterns: reversal and continuation
claim: Candlesticks reveal OHLC; hammer = small body + long lower shadow (reversal); shooting star = long upper shadow (reversal); doji = indecision
support: Pring illustrates major candlestick patterns
mechanism: Intra-bar price action signals buyer/seller control
validation: Identify candlestick patterns and measure follow-through

title: Relative strength: comparing instruments
claim: Relative Strength (RS) = price of instrument / price of benchmark; rising RS = outperformance; falling RS = underperformance
support: Pring explains RS for stock selection
mechanism: Momentum vs market reflects competitive strength
validation: Compute RS ratio and identify consistent outperformers

title: DJ Transports case study 1990-2001
claim: Pring shows how to combine MA, MACD, volume, trendlines to identify trend reversals in DJ Transports index over 11-year period
support: Worked example with actual historical data
validation: Reproduce case study with updated 2015-2024 DJ Transports data

title: Major averages: S&P, Dow, Nasdaq
claim: Major averages (S&P 500, Dow Jones, Nasdaq Composite) reflect market health; all three should confirm trend; divergence signals weakness
support: Pring emphasizes multi-index confirmation
mechanism: Weak internals (few indices up) warn of reversal
validation: Compare trend signals across S&P, Dow, Nasdaq

title: Volume indicators: OBV, AD line
claim: On-Balance Volume (OBV): accumulate volume on up days, subtract on down days; AD Line: accumulate advances minus declines; confirm price trend
support: Pring explains volume indicator construction
validation: Compute OBV and AD line; measure divergence signals

title: Market breadth: advance/decline ratio
claim: Breadth = # advancing issues / # declining; breadth above 2.0 = strong uptrend; below 0.5 = weak; divergence with price warns of reversal
support: Pring explains market breadth interpretation
validation: Calculate A/D ratio from exchange data; measure predictive power

title: Confidence indicators: Junk bond spread
claim: Junk bond yield spread over Treasuries reflects risk appetite; widening spread = falling confidence = equity decline risk
support: Pring explains bond market confidence signals
mechanism: Yield spread reflects investor risk tolerance
validation: Monitor HY-OAS (high yield OAS) and measure correlation to equity drawdowns

title: Sentiment: contrarian indicator
claim: Extreme bullish sentiment (> 70 percent bulls) often precedes correction; extreme bearish (< 20 percent bulls) precedes rally; sentiment is contrarian
support: Pring discusses sentiment surveys (AAII, Market Vane)
validation: Track AAII percent bulls weekly; measure accuracy of sentiment reversals

title: Interest rates: inverse equity relationship
claim: Rising interest rates reduce equity valuations; falling rates support equity prices; real rates (nominal - inflation) key
support: Pring explains Fed rate impact on equities
mechanism: Discount rate increases; bond yields compete with stocks
validation: Correlate 10Y rate changes to SPX returns; measure significance

title: Stock selection via relative strength
claim: Combine market timing (index) with RS to select leading stocks; stocks with rising RS outperform in bull markets
support: Pring demonstrates stock selection process
validation: Backtest: select top 10 stocks by RS in bull market; measure alpha

title: Automated trading systems: rule-based entry/exit
claim: Systematic trading removes emotion; rules based on indicators (MA, MACD, RSI) generate signals; backtest before live trading
support: Pring advocates for rule-based trading
validation: Define rules; backtest; measure Sharpe, max DD, win rate

title: Primary peak/trough identification checklist
claim: Pring provides checklist for identifying primary reversals: trend break, MA cross, momentum divergence, volume confirmation, sentiment extreme
support: Multi-factor confirmation framework
validation: Apply checklist to historical reversals; measure hit rate

title: Multi-indicator confirmation improves signal quality
claim: Combining trendline break + MA crossover + MACD signal + volume surge should yield higher win rate than individual indicators
support: DJ Transports case study uses multiple confirmations
validation: Backtest: individual rules vs combined; measure win rate, payoff ratio

title: Support/resistance holds in regime transitions
claim: Support levels from prior swings predict future price lows within regime; hypothesis: price never falls more than 2x distance to nearest prior support
support: Pring support/resistance theory
mechanism: Psychological price levels and order clustering
validation: Historical backtest: identify support; measure holds vs penetrations

title: Regime detection: volatility as proxy
claim: Rising volatility (BB band width) signals regime change; system should adapt stops, position size, signal threshold based on regime
support: Pring notes BB volatility signals
mechanism: High vol = breakout regime; low vol = range-bound
validation: Compare signal metrics (win rate, DD, payoff) in high/low vol regimes
